findings.finding: The active retrieval check (check-what-was-lost) immediately forces the learner to commit to comparing the lossy shorthand note with the detailed observation log. This sets a strong cognitive foundation for the rest of the lesson.

The clinical wrap-up scene successfully transfers and motivates the lesson's main ideas. By explaining how the diagnostic label 'psychomotor retardation' can mask a physiological thyroid condition (hypothyroidism), the lesson provides a highly compelling answer to why descriptive accuracy matters in clinical records.

The definition-mood-and-affect block clearly separates reported mood from observed affect, providing a crisp heuristic ('One is reported. The other is watched. Neither is evidence for the other.') that effectively addresses a common source of confusion for medical novices.

limitations: Evaluated strictly from a learning design perspective. Clinical validity of psychiatric assessments and medical facts was not audited, as that falls under the academic reviewer role. Legal boundaries concerning copy permissions or local service regulations were not reviewed.
